provenance.scope: A film the museum made of what a work describes, shown as that work's close look. Its lines run under the film, outside the picture: each from its own second of the film until the next line's. The work's own line in lines.json stays the work's.
provenance.rule: A line holds at most 120 characters and 20 words in either language, and no sentence over 14 words. Every line names its source, and the record prints it.
provenance.files: The film's bytes live in the asset store. A record there names this file's key as its `source`, its role (`showpiece-film` or `showpiece-poster`) and its framing; a work whose records the store does not carry opens as it did before.
provenance.extent: Where the model stands in a framing's frame over the run, as shares of the frame [left, top, right, bottom]: the union of the glass's box in every frame where it stands whole (its edges, so a lit wall does not count), read from the film's own frames at two a second. Where the camera is inside it (the frame filled), the same box is shown. The phone held sideways shows the film through this box.

lines.en: This is our model, built from his notes. Around 1512 he drew the water curling behind the flaps.
lines.de: Das ist unser Modell nach seinen Notizen. Um 1512 zeichnete er, wie das Wasser hinter der Klappe wirbelt.

lines.en: Those curls help shut the valve, as he wrote. Seen in a model in 1968, in one person in 2014.
lines.de: Diese Wirbel helfen der Klappe beim Schließen, wie er schrieb. 1968 sah man sie im Modell, 2014 bei einem Menschen.
lines.source: Bellhouse and Bellhouse, Nature 217 (1968). Bissell, Dall'Armellina and Choudhury, European Heart Journal 35 (2014).
